By the Crystal Pier, a Pacific Beach Breakfast Spot That Never Needs an Introduction

By There San Diego Staff · San Diego

Walk the boardwalk far enough north in Pacific Beach and you will hit a line before you hit the ocean. That line belongs to Kono's Cafe, the cafe parked right at the foot of Crystal Pier on Garnet Avenue, where the sand starts and the day's first cup of coffee usually gets poured. It is a cafe in the plainest sense of the word: food and beverages, served casually, to whoever wanders in off the beach or in from the neighborhood.

Right Where Garnet Avenue Meets the Sand

The address, 704 Garnet Ave, puts Kono's at the exact spot where Pacific Beach stops being a street grid and starts being a coastline. It is the kind of location that does a lot of the work on its own: order at the counter, then find a spot to eat with a view of the pier and the water. That geography is a big part of why the place has become a fixture rather than just another storefront on the strip.

konitoscafe
Pacific Beach

A Cafe Built for the Way People Actually Eat at the Beach

Kono's keeps its job simple and does it well: cafe dining, food service, and beverages, all built around a casual dining atmosphere that does not ask anything of you beyond showing up hungry. There is no pretense in that list, and there does not need to be. It is a menu of fundamentals, served in a setting that makes the fundamentals feel like enough.

Kono's Cafe is a cafe located in Pacific Beach, San Diego, serving food and beverages to customers in a casual dining atmosphere.

That description, plain as it is, explains the draw. This is not a place chasing trends in the coffee world or reinventing the diner plate. It is a neighborhood cafe doing cafe things, in a location that happens to be one of the best in San Diego for doing them.

What Makes the Trip Worth It

The pull here is the combination, not any single dish or drink: casual food, real beverages, and a spot to eat them with Crystal Pier and the Pacific Beach shoreline right there. It is the kind of setup that turns a coffee run into a reason to linger, especially on a clear morning when the pier is doing its postcard thing in the background.

Kono's has built up a following that shows in the numbers: ★ 4.8 (2929 reviews), a track record that few cafes in Pacific Beach can match. That kind of volume, sustained over time, tends to mean the crowd at the counter is as much local as it is tourist, and both keep coming back.

How to Do Your First Visit Right

Show up ready to order at the counter, grab your food and drinks, and take them outside if the weather is doing what Pacific Beach weather usually does. Come early if the idea of a line bothers you, since the boardwalk location means Kono's gets discovered by anyone walking the pier area. From there, it is a straightforward cafe visit: casual, quick, and better with an ocean view than it would be anywhere else.

If breakfast by the water is on your list this week, Kono's Cafe is the place to point yourself toward. Visit at Crystal Pier for fresh cafe food and drinks in Pacific Beach, and check konoscafepb.com before you go for anything new on the counter.
